newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee firm but off highs after NY gyrations.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee firm but off highs after NY gyrations.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures headed lower in solid afternoon trade on Wednesday in a milder reflection of the gyrations of the arabicas market, beset by supply fears and low stocks.
During London's session, New York's key July contract see-sawed in a wide range between 248.50 and 236.00 cents per lb and traders said prices in London were also erratic but were not so volatile.
"It's unreal...people can't take a daily view on this market, they have to take an hourly view," said one.
Roasters dominated on the buy side in London, although trade and speculative interest was also noted. Trade players were the day's prominent sellers.

Earlier in the day, origin offers capped the gains racked up by the July robusta contract, which surged nearly four percent to score a fresh one-year high on fund buying and manufacturer position-covering.
"Overall the picture is still looking very rosy and you have to go with the flow. Everything is still pointing higher," the trader said, adding that Brazil's frost season was still some way away.
Both markets are bracing for frost scares from Brazil as winter sets in from late May.
At the close benchmark July was up $53 at $1,870 after its earlier peak of $1,885. All positions ended firmer and overall volume amounted to 8,836 lots.
Traders said robustas were poised for further upward progress, with July's initial upside objective seen at between $1,920 and $1,930.
In other news, Ivory Coast's Commodities Minister said in an interview coffee output in the Oct/Sept 1996/97 season would be less than 300,000 tonnes.

Ivorian coffee exporters have said that green coffee arrivals at its ports have already totalled around 250,000 tonnes by May 9 in the current season against 180,000 tonnes at the same time last year.
